Higher rated voltage means less capacitance lost to DC bias on every rail these sit on, and the automotive grade is screened harder. 1,435,431 in stock, $0.17 (verified 2026-08-19). ECO-10 (proposed in the power review, deferred by ECO-8, applied here). X7R -> C0G. These are the Sallen-Key FEEDBACK caps -- the ones that set Q -- and their partners C26/C31 are already C0G. X7R drifts +/-15% over its range while C0G drifts +/-30ppm/degC, so a handheld warming in the hand detunes half of each filter section and no tolerance grade fixes it.
ECO-10. Already C0G; tolerance +/-5% -> +/-1%, and AEC-Q200. Q goes as sqrt(Cfb/Cgnd), so tightening the shunt legs tightens the alignment directly.
ECO-10. Same as C24/C32: the other feedback pair, X7R -> C0G.

ECO-10. FEEDFORWARD caps across the top leg of each divider (VOUT -> FB, verified from the netlist), so the zero they set is 1/(2*pi*R_top*C). Dropping R_top 10x without touching C would move it from ~6 kHz to ~60 kHz and discard the phase lead it exists to provide, so 15 pF -> 150 pF holds it where the design put it. The datasheet says only that 'a typical value of 15pF will generally suffice', so this preserves MouseBiteLabs' compensation rather than following a mandate. C0G +/-1% 100 V AEC-Q200 -- a compensation element should not drift with temperature.

ECO-10. The LTC3527 specifies FB input current as 1 nA typ / 50 nA MAX. With the original 1.69M/1.00M and 1.78M/560k dividers that worst case moves VOUT3 by +/-85 mV (+/-2.62%) and VOUT5 by +/-89 mV (+/-1.77%) -- more than the resistors' own tolerance, and more than the 108 mV ECO-8 trimmed off VOUT3 to save 6.1 mW. Scaling both dividers 10x down keeps the ratio and therefore the rail, cuts the bias error to +/-8.4 / +/-8.9 mV, and lands on values where 0.1% +/-25ppm thin film exists -- which it does not at 1.69M or 1.78M, because nobody builds precision resistors that high for exactly this reason. Costs 0.13 mW of extra divider current. All four legs are YAGEO RT0603 so both dividers track on ONE film system. R21 = VOUT5 top leg, was 1.78M.

ECO-10, audio precision. These set f0 and Q of the 4th-order Butterworth reconstruction filter (15.84 kHz per channel). 1% +/-100ppm thick film -> 0.1% +/-25ppm thin film. Susumu RG1608 covers every value in the filter, so the whole network is ONE film system and the ratios that set Q track each other instead of drifting independently. ~$0.11 a part. R58 is not in the filter -- it is the U17 supervisor's upper divider leg, and it gets the same part for the same reason: a trip point should not move with temperature.

ECO-8: replaces 100k on the MIC1553 CS pull-up. 470k not the 1M the review proposed: the MIC1553 datasheet gives no numeric CS leakage spec and warns that a floating CS is unpredictable, and the worst-case CS-high threshold is 0.72 x VS = 3.61 V, not the nominal 2/3.
Schematic value 'CSS-1310B' is an incomplete ordering code. The orderable part is CSS-1310TB.
Confirms this is an oscillator, not a power switch -- the MIC1553 is an IttyBitty RC 555-type astable. It drives the low-battery LED blink.
TPS22917DBVT is the same die on a different reel; see `alternate`. Which of the two to order is a stock question, not an engineering one.

The most expensive active on the board by a wide margin, and the LTC3527 is the converter the power review's Tier-2 recommends transplanting for a TPS63802. Cost argues the same way efficiency does -- check the live price block below before treating that as settled.
